gemma4_verdict: google/gemma-4-31B-it (dense) runs well on 32 GB non-CUDA hardware. The Q4_K_M GGUF is ~18 GB, leaving ~14 GB headroom on a 32 GB card for KV cache and context. Unsloth ships verified GGUF quants (Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, UD-IQ4_NL, UD-Q4_K_XL). On AMD ROCm there is one notable known issue: some users report token corruption / garbage output (e.g. '<|channel><unused49>...') with certain Gemma 4 GGUF quants under ROCm/HIP that does NOT appear under the Vulkan (RADV) backend or with ggml-org's own quants — a backend-specific bug, not a model defect. The dense 31B works fine with llama-server using UD-IQ4_NL once a good quant is chosen. On Apple Silicon, Gemma 4 31B Q4 needs at least 36 GB unified memory (48 GB recommended for Q5 plus context); Ollama is currently the most stable runtime for Gemma 4 31B while MLX is theoretically faster but support was still maturing as of mid-2026. Because Gemma 4 31B is DENSE (all 31B params active), it is more memory-bandwidth-bound than an MoE of the same size — speed depends heavily on the card's bandwidth.
qwen3_verdict: Qwen/Qwen3-32B (dense, text-only) also fits comfortably on 32 GB non-CUDA cards at Q4_K_M (~18-20 GB). GGUF quants are widely available (Unsloth, bartowski, official) and are mature on both ROCm and Metal. AMD has invested heavily in the Qwen line: it announced Day-0 vLLM/ROCm support for newer Qwen3-Coder family models on Instinct GPUs, and the broader Qwen3 family is among the best-tested open-weight models on AMD. On Apple Silicon, Qwen3-32B dense runs via MLX (mlx-community quants) and llama.cpp; the MoE siblings (e.g. Qwen3.x-35B-A3B with ~3.3B active params) are dramatically faster on the same hardware (64-92 tok/s on M4 Max vs slower dense decode) and fit in 32 GB at higher quant. As a dense 32B, Qwen3-32B has the same bandwidth-bound throughput characteristics as Gemma 4 31B. [uncertain] No single source benchmarked Gemma 4 31B and Qwen3-32B head-to-head on identical 32 GB ROCm/Metal hardware.
benchmarks: This dimension is hardware/deployment, not capability — task accuracy benchmarks (GPQA, MMLU-Pro, etc.) do not differentiate the two models here. The relevant performance benchmarks are throughput: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (RDNA4, 32 GB) hits ~99 tok/s decode on a 7-8B-class model and ~48-72 tok/s decode on a 27-32B-class model with llama.cpp; Apple M4 Max reaches ~64-92 tok/s on MoE 35B-A3B and high-tens tok/s on dense 31B/32B at Q4. RX 7900 XTX (24 GB, too small for these 32B models without offload) reaches ~96 tok/s on Llama 3.1 8B (~75% of RTX 4090). [uncertain] No dense-32B tok/s numbers split out specifically by Gemma 4 31B vs Qwen3-32B on the same card.
factual_accuracy: Not applicable to the deployment dimension — quantization choice, not model identity, drives any accuracy delta here. Practical guidance from the field: Q4_K_M is the recommended balance for 32 GB hardware; Q5_K_M or Q8 (where 48 GB Apple memory allows) reduces quantization-induced quality loss on edge cases. The dominant risk on this dimension is the ROCm Gemma 4 token-corruption bug, which produces garbage tokens (a deployment failure, not a hallucination) — mitigated by choosing a known-good quant (UD-IQ4_NL / ggml-org) or the Vulkan backend.
inference_speed: Best 32 GB non-CUDA options ranked by tok/s for a dense 31-32B model at Q4: (1) AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (RDNA4, 32 GB GDDR6, 640 GB/s, ~$1,250-1,300) — ~48-72 tok/s decode on a 27-32B dense model with llama.cpp; Vulkan backend often FASTER than ROCm HIP on RDNA4 (~183 vs ~150 tok/s decode on smaller models) because Vulkan uses KHR_cooperative_matrix for the RDNA4 matrix cores; dual-R9700 with tensor-split + MTP reaches 1000+ tok/s prefill and 58-72 tok/s decode. (2) Apple M4 Max 48 GB (~546 GB/s, ~$2,600+) — high-tens tok/s on dense 31B/32B Q4, 64-92 tok/s on MoE 35B-A3B; MLX is 20-87% faster than llama.cpp for sub-14B but advantage shrinks at 31B+. (3) AMD Radeon Pro W7800 (RDNA3, 32 GB, ~$2,500 MSRP) — roughly RTX 3090-class, ROCm llama.cpp ~70-80% of CUDA speed at equal bandwidth. (4) AMD Radeon Pro W6800 (RDNA2, 32 GB, ~$1,350 used) — slowest of the group (~34 tok/s class on RDNA2 generation). MoE variants of either model line would be markedly faster than dense; MTP speculative decoding helps prefill notably on dual-GPU ROCm.
multimodal_support: Deployment-relevant note: Gemma 4 31B is multimodal (image input) per its model line, but multimodal inference through llama.cpp/GGUF requires the separate mmproj projector file and has historically lagged text-only support across non-CUDA backends — verify the vision path works on ROCm/Metal before relying on it. Qwen3-32B base is text-only (the VL capability is a separate Qwen model line), so on this dimension Qwen3-32B has no multimodal deployment concern but also no multimodal capability. For figure-heavy academic paper reading, Gemma 4 is the only candidate of the two, contingent on the GGUF vision path working on the chosen backend. [uncertain]
context_window: Deployment constraint: on a 32 GB card running a ~18 GB Q4 model, only ~14 GB remains for KV cache, which caps practical context. Field defaults use -c 8192 to -c 16384 on 32 GB hardware; reaching 32k+ context for a full literature-review session may require dropping to a smaller quant (Q3/IQ4) or using flash-attention/KV-cache compression. RDNA3+ supports rocWMMA flash attention (-DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON) which reduces KV memory pressure. FP8 KV-cache quantization is NOT available on RDNA3 (weak), limiting the cheapest context-extension trick available on NVIDIA. Apple 48 GB unified memory gives the most context headroom of the affordable options.
non_cuda_support: Confirmed working 32 GB non-CUDA GPUs for these models in 2026: (A) AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 — RDNA4 (gfx1201), 32 GB GDDR6, 640 GB/s, ~$1,244-1,299; best price/VRAM, fastest of the AMD options, works via llama.cpp ROCm HIP AND Vulkan (Vulkan often faster on RDNA4). Known issue: HIP backend keeps GPU pinned at 100% / non-idle after load until llama-server exits (ROCm 7.1.x bug; Vulkan unaffected). (B) AMD Radeon Pro W7800 — RDNA3 (gfx1100), 32 GB GDDR6 ECC, ~$2,500 MSRP (street ~$1,700-4,000), ~RTX 3090-class, mature ROCm. (C) AMD Radeon Pro W6800 — RDNA2, 32 GB, ~$1,350 used, slowest. (D) Apple M3/M4 Max 36-48 GB unified (~$2,100-2,600+) and M4 Pro 48 GB Mac Mini (~$1,999) — Metal/MLX + llama.cpp, 48 GB is the sweet spot for 31-32B at Q4/Q5. There is NO 32 GB RX 9070 XT consumer variant (16 GB only); the R9700 is the RDNA4 32 GB card. RX 7900 XTX is 24 GB (too small for these dense 32B models without CPU offload). GGUF quants for both models are available and working. Build complexity: AMD requires ROCm 7.x + cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100 (RDNA3) or -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1201 (RDNA4); add -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON for flash attention. Known build pitfalls: rocWMMA compile errors on Ubuntu 24.04 + ROCm 6.4 + gfx1100; iGPU crashes mitigated with HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0. Apple build is trivial (Metal is default in llama.cpp / use mlx-lm). Prebuilt ROCm llama.cpp binaries are published by AMD.
over_refusal_risk: Not applicable to the deployment dimension — refusal behavior is model-policy, not backend-dependent, and is unaffected by running on ROCm/Metal vs CUDA. No deployment-specific refusal concern for either model on non-CUDA hardware.
ecosystem_toolchain: Non-CUDA toolchain maturity (2026): llama.cpp has the broadest non-CUDA coverage — ROCm HIP build for RDNA2/3/4, Vulkan backend (frequently the better choice on RDNA4), and Metal on Apple; AMD publishes prebuilt ROCm llama.cpp binaries and ROCm-versioned docs. Ollama and LM Studio both run on ROCm and Metal and are the most stable runtimes for Gemma 4 31B specifically. MLX / mlx-lm provides the fastest Apple-Silicon path (quants on mlx-community / unsloth) but Gemma 4 support was still catching up vs Ollama as of mid-2026. vLLM ROCm reached genuine inference maturity in 2026 (ROCm 7.2.x in production, 7.13 preview): MI300X uses CK attention kernels, RDNA3/4 (RX 7900 XTX, RX 9070 XT, R9700) use Triton attention; FlashAttention-2 has an official AMD port for RDNA3/CDNA3. vLLM tool-call parser flag is 'gemma4' for Gemma 4 (vs 'pythonic' for Gemma 3) and 'hermes' for Qwen3 — this is backend-agnostic. AMD gives the Qwen line Day-0 vLLM support on Instinct GPUs. Remaining gaps on consumer AMD: FP8 software weak on RDNA3 (fine on MI300), no FP8 KV-cache quant, training tooling still NVIDIA-favored, limited Windows-native support (use WSL2). Net: for single 32 GB card inference, llama.cpp (ROCm or Vulkan) and Ollama are the pragmatic choice; vLLM ROCm is viable but better justified on Instinct / multi-GPU.
labmate_relevance: HIGH. Labmate is explicitly targeted at a single-GPU 32 GB non-CUDA host (per CLAUDE.md and the M3+ vLLM-on-host design), and must run both the Gemma 4 31B orchestrator brain and a 32B specialist. Whether/how both 32B-class models can be served on affordable non-CUDA hardware is a gating deployment decision for the entire project.
recommendation: For a 32 GB non-CUDA host running both Gemma 4 31B and Qwen3-32B, the standout value pick is the AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (RDNA4, 32 GB, ~$1,250-1,300): RTX 5090-class VRAM at ~1/3 the price, ~48-72 tok/s decode on dense 31-32B at Q4, and — importantly — use the VULKAN backend rather than ROCm HIP on RDNA4 (faster, and it avoids the HIP 100%-idle and Gemma-4 token-corruption bugs). For users wanting a quieter / unified-memory machine, an Apple M4 Max 48 GB (or M4 Pro 48 GB Mac Mini at ~$1,999) runs both models at Q4/Q5 with the most context headroom; use Ollama for Gemma 4 31B today and MLX where it is stable. The Radeon Pro W7800 (RDNA3, 32 GB) is a solid but pricier mature-ROCm fallback; the W6800 is the budget-but-slow option. Serving strategy: run a single dense 32B model at a time per 32 GB card (each ~18 GB Q4 + KV cache leaves no room to co-resident both); to host both simultaneously, use two R9700s (tensor-split + MTP gives 1000+ tok/s prefill) or swap models. Prefer Gemma 4 31B when figure/document multimodal reading is needed (verify the GGUF vision path on your backend first); either model is fine for pure-text reasoning, with Qwen3 enjoying slightly stronger AMD/vLLM day-0 ecosystem support. Use llama.cpp built with -DGGML_HIP=ON + -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON on RDNA3, or the Vulkan build on RDNA4; pin a known-good Gemma 4 quant (UD-IQ4_NL).
